problem:
In a factory, the amount of sugar on a cookie is normally distributed with a mean of $15$ grams and a standard deviation of $0.8$ grams. What is the probability that the amount of sugar on a randomly selected cookie is less than $14$ grams? Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.

*Hint: A table of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\,0.03\,$ | $\,0.04\,$ | $\,0.05\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,-1.2\,$ | $\,0.1093\,$ | $\,0.1075\,$ | $\,0.1056\,$ |
| $\,-1.1\,$ | $\,0.1292\,$ | $\,0.1271\,$ | $\,0.1251\,$ |
| $\,-1.0\,$ | $\,0.1515\,$ | $\,0.1492\,$ | $\,0.1469\,$ |
worked_solution:
Let $X$ represent the amount of sugar (in grams) on the cookies. Then we have $X∼N(15,{0.8}^{2}).$

We want to find $P(X<14).$ First, we write this as a cumulative probability:

$$
P(X<14)=P(X\le 14)
$$

Then, we convert $X$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 14) & =P(Z\le \frac{14-15}{0.8}) \\  & =P(Z\le -1.25) \\  & =Φ(-1.25)\end{aligned}
$$

From the $z$-table, we see that

$$
Φ(-1.25)=0.1056≈0.11.
$$

Therefore, the probability that the amount of sugar on a randomly selected cookie is less than $14$ grams is approximately $0.11.$
